messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rate detected for model-serving cluster us-west-2-prod (alerts: 4xx spike, routing failures). Pager: sara (oncall). Severity: P1.

sara (oncall): Ack'd. I'm on it — pulling logs now. ETA 5m to triage.

devops-pager: Routing alert context:
- cluster: us-west-2-prod
- affected routes: /v1/generate (customer tier: enterprise)
- 5xx rate: 18% over 2m window
- recent deploy? no deploys in last 30m

liam (engineer): Joining. Saw a kube restart for model-worker-3 around T-3m on the node. Might be OOM or NVLINK flapping.

maya (eng-sre): Added flamegraph and tail of runtime logs to the thread:
```
[2023-11-09T10:02:13Z] model-worker-3 ERROR kv-cache: Failed to mmap cache segment: Input/output error
[2023-11-09T10:02:14Z] runtime serving ERROR read error: connection reset by peer
```

sara (oncall): Observed increased client retries from two enterprise customers: Aventis Health (acct: aventis-prod) and KestrelPay (acct: kestrel-enterprise). Both are routed to dedicated capacity in us-west-2.

ellie (customer-success): Copy — I'm prepping customer comms. Quick ask: can we get a tailored impact statement for Aventis? They have live clinical ingest jobs; we need precise scope.

jordan (support): Aventis escalation: primary contacts on file — Dr. Priya Nambiar (priya.n@aventis.com) and ops lead Marco Ruiz (marco.r@aventis.com). They reported timeouts starting ~T-4m. I've opened a ticket: AV-4512.

liam (engineer): Root cause hypothesis: one of the model workers hit a corrupted mmap for the prefix cache on nvme which caused the worker to crash loop, triggering routing to lower-tier pools which then saturated and produced retries/timeouts.

maya (eng-sre): Confirmed worker crashloop on node ip 10.20.3.12. Kernel logs show I/O errors to /dev/nvme1n1. Initiating node cordon and draining affected pods.

devops-pager: Action checklist (in-flight):
1) cordon/evict pods from 10.20.3.12 (maya) -> in progress
2) scale up warm pool for dedicated us-west-2 by +3 pods (liam) -> started
3) route critical enterprise traffic to fallback pool (policy: enterprise-fallback) (sara) -> will execute after warm pool up
4) draft status page + customer emails (ellie/jordan) -> waiting for impact text

sara (oncall): Rolling routing change to enterprise-fallback for Aventis and Kestrel now (5% canary for 60s, then 100% if no regressions). Notifying monitoring.

incident-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: enterprise-fallback -> canary 5% -> user groups: aventis-prod, kestrel-enterprise.

liam (engineer): Warm pool scaled. New pods healthy. Canary routing shows successful requests for sample traffic. Error rate dropped from 18% to 2% on canary.

maya (eng-sre): Drain complete on 10.20.3.12. Disk SMART shows reallocated sectors and I/O errors — NVMe likely failing. Node will be quarantined.

anna (ops-manager): Good catch. We'll mark node for replacement. Does this change customer impact messaging?

liam (engineer): Impact narrowed: only enterprise customers pinned to that physical node's shard experienced degraded requests. Failure did not affect control plane or hosted shared customers.

ellie (customer-success): Drafted tailored impact statements below — please confirm factual bits, then I will send to Aventis and Kestrel via their escalation paths and post an interim status page update.

ellie (customer-success): Aventis impact draft:
"Dear Priya / Marco,
We experienced a transient interruption to dedicated inference capacity in us-west-2 between ~10:01–10:10 UTC which caused increased timeouts and retries for some inference calls. Impact: clinical ingest and inference jobs routed to aventis-prod saw elevated error rates and occasional timeouts; non-routed jobs and the control plane were not affected. Mitigation: traffic has been moved to a fallback dedicated pool and degraded node has been quarantined; we are replacing the faulty storage device. Next steps: postmortem and follow-up with exact token-level traces within 48 hours. We apologize for the disruption and are standing by for any questions. — Redwood Inference Ops & Customer Success"

ellie (customer-success): KestrelPay impact draft:
"Hi team,
Between ~10:01–10:10 UTC your dedicated inference capacity in us-west-2 experienced elevated error rates due to an underlying host storage failure. We rerouted traffic and restored successful request rates; we do not expect any lasting data loss. Full root cause analysis and remediation timeline will follow. — Redwood Inference"

sara (oncall): Confirm the times and that the fallback routing completed by 10:06 UTC. Also state that we throttled retries to prevent cascading load.

liam (engineer): Confirmed: canary roll started 10:04, full fallback by 10:06. We also tightened retry policy to max_retries=1 for the affected routes to prevent amplification.

ellie (customer-success): Updated drafts with times and retry policy note. Preparing two outbound emails and a status page entry. Proposed status page (interim):
```markdown
Incident: Dedicated capacity degradation (us-west-2)
Status: Identified / Mitigated
Start: 2026-03-15T10:01:00Z
End: 2026-03-15T10:10:00Z
Impact: Increased error rates and timeouts for some enterprise customers on dedicated pools in us-west-2. Affected customers: Aventis Health (aventis-prod), KestrelPay (kestrel-enterprise).
Current status: Traffic rerouted to fallback pools; affected host quarantined; device replacement scheduled.
Next update: After RCA within 48hrs.
```

jordan (support): I'll queue the Aventis and Kestrel templates in the outbound escalate channel and attach the ticket IDs. Also pinging account execs.

anna (ops-manager): Approve sending to customers with the current wording. Add: "We will provide a timeline for device replacement in the RCA."

ellie (customer-success): Sent to Aventis (cc: account exec, legal) to priya.n@aventis.com and marco.r@aventis.com. Copy of message posted to support ticket AV-4512.

ellie (customer-success): Sent to Kestrel ops contact and attached ticket KP-778.

incident-bot: OUTBOUND EMAIL LOGGED: Aventis Health (AV-4512) KestrelPay (KP-778).

sara (oncall): Handing off incident to liam for investigation and RCA. I'm moving to watch for regressions but going offline for a shift; liam, take incident leadership.

liam (engineer): Taking lead. I'll collect traces, node metrics, and disk vendor logs for RCA. Expected 24–48h for full report; will surface interim timeline ASAP.

maya (eng-sre): Added runbook pointers and commands used during mitigation:
```bash
# cordon & drain
kubectl cordon node-10.20.3.12
kubectl drain node-10.20.3.12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# scale warm pool
kubectl scale deployment/dedicated-warm --replicas=+3 -n serving
```

ellie (customer-success): Customer outreach summary (internal):
- Aventis (primary): notified 10:12 UTC via email, ticket AV-4512, CC account execs and legal.
- Kestrel (primary): notified 10:13 UTC via email, ticket KP-778.
- Status page interim posted at 10:15 UTC.

anna (ops-manager): Good work. Action items assigned:
- liam: RCA and disk vendor engagement (owner)
- maya: node replacement and fleet health check (owner)
- sara: monitoring tweaks and retry guardrails follow-up (owner)
- ellie/jordan: customer comm follow-through and templates (owner)

devops-pager: NOTE: For enterprise routing playbook, add step to proactively warm fallback pools when any shard shows I/O errors. Filing follow-up ticket: INF-9052.

liam (engineer): I'll attach perf traces and a minimum-repro script to the RCA. Expect preliminary findings in 6–8 hours.

sara (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated in channel. Will update on-call log and handoff notes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status changed to MITIGATED by sara (oncall).

ellie (customer-success): Final internal note: if customers request SLA credits, route to revenue ops and legal with ticket references.

jordan (support): Logged customer replies. Aventis confirmed they saw improved metrics and accepted interim update. Kestrel acknowledged.

liam (engineer): Leaving this thread for RCA documentation. Ping me if anything regress.

sara (oncall): Thanks team — nice quick mitigation. :thumbsup:
